headline: Curated cross-species databases expand annotation of miRNAs, snoRNAs, and RBP target sites
label: Multispecies Noncoding Rna Resources
summary: Four 2026 database releases broaden cross-species coverage of miRNA, snoRNA, and RBP target annotation in model organisms.
synthesis: The dominant thread is curated, cross-species annotation of regulatory RNAs. DIANA-miRGen v5 characterizes miRNA transcription start sites and host/promoter contexts in human and mouse, drawing on CLS long-read data, GENCODE, and CAGE. miRPathDB 2027 extends miRNA-pathway association evidence to rat and rhesus macaque, with three evidence tiers and cross-species views. SnoDB 3.0 adds mouse annotations to human snoRNA records, with updated interactors and cross-species snoRNA and rRNA target correspondence. oRNAment V2 expands putative RNA binding protein target sites across the transcriptomes of diverse model species. What is new is broader species coverage and explicit evidence tiering, with versioned downloads supporting reuse. These items are database resources rather than experimental studies, so their shared contribution is infrastructure for regulatory RNA annotation across organisms.
